h: Gardens, Trails and a Gatwick Twist
p: Crawley sits in a surprisingly green bit of West Sussex, and some of the county's finest gardens are just a short hop from Tilgate. Nymans at Handcross, the National Trust garden with its romantic ruined house, is gorgeous in spring and summer. Wakehurst near Ardingly, Kew's wild botanic garden in the countryside, is another brilliant follow-up, with woodland, wetlands and the Millennium Seed Bank to explore.
If your crew prefers two wheels, the Worth Way follows an old railway line east from Three Bridges towards East Grinstead, giving you a flat, traffic-free ride or walk through the countryside.

For the treetop bit, plan on a couple of hours once you're kitted up. Arrive early enough to park and find the meeting point without a mad dash, especially on summer weekends when Tilgate is busy with families. A small backpack with water and snacks is handy, though you'll be leaving it on the ground while you climb.

Little tip for nervous first-timers: talk your way through it. Saying out loud which clip goes where helps keep the routine steady and calms the nerves. And if you're flying out of Gatwick, a morning on the ropes is a surprisingly good way to wear the kids out before a long flight, as long as you leave plenty of margin to get to the terminal.
